behavior_constraints: Every detect anomaly JSON object has a top-level evidence field sibling of id, type, severity, details, and source; not nested in details.
For gradient_spike anomalies, evidence.window_values is an array of up to 5 preceding grad_norm values at the detection point.
For loss_divergence anomalies, evidence.window_values is an array of up to 5 preceding loss values at the detection point.
Other timeline-based detect anomalies include evidence.window_values when meaningful; an empty array is acceptable when no preceding metric window exists.
Checkpoint-based detect anomalies such as tensor_checksum_mismatch have evidence as an empty object: {}.
detect --format csv outputs exactly the header id,type,severity,epoch,step,source,checkpoint followed by one data row per anomaly with 7 comma-separated fields in that order.
CSV rows leave epoch, step, or checkpoint empty when the anomaly lacks that field.
detect --filter-severity LEVEL filters anomalies to only those at the specified severity or above, using order critical > high > medium > low.
--filter-severity high shows critical and high; --filter-severity critical shows only critical; the JSON summary reflects the filtered anomaly list.
JSON output structure for all commands other than detect remains unchanged.
